{{short description|Conjecture in group theory}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Sims conjecture''' is a result in [[group theory]], originally proposed by [[Charles Sims (mathematician)|Charles Sims]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Sims |first=Charles C. |authorlink=Charles Sims (mathematician) |title=Graphs and finite permutation groups |journal=[[Mathematische Zeitschrift]] |volume=95 |number=1 |year=1967 |pages=76–86 |doi=10.1007/BF01117534|s2cid=186227555 }}</ref> He [[conjecture]]d that if <math>G</math> is a [[primitive permutation group]] on a finite set <math>S</math> and <math>G_\alpha</math> denotes the [[stabilizer (group theory)|stabilizer]] of the point <math>\alpha</math> in <math>S</math>, then there exists an [[integer]]-valued [[function (mathematics)|function]] <math>f</math> such that <math>f(d) \geq |G_\alpha|</math> for <math>d</math> the length of any [[orbit (group theory)|orbit]] of <math>G_\alpha</math> in the set <math>S \setminus \{\alpha\}</math>. 

The conjecture was [[mathematical proof|proven]] by [[Peter Cameron (mathematician)|Peter Cameron]], [[Cheryl Praeger]], [[Jan Saxl]], and [[Gary Seitz]] using the [[classification of finite simple groups]], in particular the fact that only finitely many [[isomorphism]] types of [[sporadic group]]s exist.

The theorem reads precisely as follows.<ref>{{Cite arXiv|eprint = 2102.06670|last1 = Pyber|first1 = László|last2 = Tracey|first2 = Gareth|title = Some simplifications in the proof of the Sims conjecture|year = 2021| class=math.GR }}</ref>

{{math theorem|There exists a function <math>f: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} </math> such that whenever <math>G</math> is a primitive permutation group and <math>h > 1</math> is the length of a non-trivial orbit of a point stabilizer <math>H</math> in <math>G</math>, then the [[order (group theory)|order]] of <math>H</math> is at most <math>f(h)</math>.}}

Thus, in a primitive permutation group with "large" stabilizers, these stabilizers cannot have any small orbit.  A consequence of their proof is that there exist only finitely many [[connectivity (graph theory)|connected]] [[distance-transitive graph|distance-transitive]] [[graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]]s having [[degree (graph theory)|degree]] greater than 2.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Cameron |first1=Peter J. |last2=Praeger |first2=Cheryl E. |last3=Saxl |first3=Jan |last4=Seitz |first4=Gary M. |authorlink1=Peter Cameron (mathematician) |authorlink2=Cheryl Praeger |author3-link=Jan Saxl|authorlink4=Gary Seitz |title=On the Sims conjecture and distance transitive graphs |journal=[[London Mathematical Society|Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society]] |volume=15 |year=1983 |issue=5 |pages=499–506 |doi=10.1112/blms/15.5.499}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Cameron |first=Peter J. |authorlink=Peter Cameron (mathematician) |title=There are only finitely many distance-transitive graphs of given valency greater than two |journal=[[Combinatorica]] |year=1982 |volume=2 |number=1 |pages=9–13 |doi=10.1007/BF02579277|s2cid=6483108 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Isaacs |first=I. Martin |authorlink=Martin Isaacs |title=Finite Group Theory |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |year=2011 |isbn=9780821843444 |oclc=935038216}}</ref>
